source.title: Dopamine encoding of novelty facilitates efficient uncertainty-driven exploration

confidence_rationale: Provides the biological grounding for MECH-343: a basal-ganglia model in which striatal pathways estimate reward mean AND variance and transient dopaminergic novelty signals drive DIRECTED (uncertainty-conditioned) exploration, which outperforms undirected and classic UCB strategies in simulation and fits behaviour. Supports the principle that exploration should be gated to a state signal rather than applied uniformly. Held to ~0.58 because the gating signal is novelty/value-uncertainty rather than goal-difficulty/stuck-state, and it is bandit-style choice rather than the sequential blocked-path setting of Q-056.
failure_signatures: Directed (uncertainty-gated) exploration outperforms undirected exploration and classic UCB in simulation -- undirected/uniform exploration is dominated.
The biological gating signal is transient novelty/value-variance, not difficulty or goal-blockage, so it does not directly evidence stuck-state gating.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Direct and indirect striatal pathways jointly estimate the mean and variance of reward, and mesolimbic dopaminergic novelty signals provide an uncertainty representation that drives efficient directed exploration -- outperforming UCB and undirected strategies in simulation and fitting behavioural data.
mapping.ree_translation: Biological precedent for MECH-343's architecture: exploration in the brain is GATED by a computed state signal (uncertainty/novelty), not delivered as a uniform constant. This supports the general claim that conditional proposal entropy is the biologically realistic and performant regime, against an always-high (undirected) alternative.
mapping.mapping_caveat: The gating variable here is reward-uncertainty / stimulus novelty, which is related to but not identical with REE's difficulty-or-stuck-state trigger; a stuck agent at a blocked goal is not necessarily in a high-novelty state. The setting is value-based action selection (bandit-like), not the sequential hard-goal/blocked-path environment Q-056 specifies, and there is no harm/safety channel.
mapping.source_context: Basal-ganglia computational model validated against rodent electrophysiology and fitted to behavioural data; simulation comparisons.

confidence_components.notes: High-quality computational-neuroscience paper (Bogacz group, PLoS Comput Biol). Mapping fidelity moderate-low: supports gating-in-general and directed>undirected, but the gating signal differs from REE's difficulty trigger.
